Hi Alice / Carlos — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side:

- Scope: production chat/summarization workload (avg 1.2k tokens/session, 99th latency SLO 500ms).
- Immediate asks we captured: sample prompt set, preferred quality thresholds, and any regulatory constraints on quantized model artifacts.

What we recommended on the call:
1) Model candidates to evaluate: Llama-3-13B (FP16 baseline), Redoak-7B (AWQ, lower-cost), and a 13B GPTQ quantized variant for mid-point.
2) Eval plan: run your prompt set (~500 canonical sessions) through each variant for pass/fail on quality regression + throughput numbers. We'll produce per-token latency & cost estimates.
3) Canary/rollout suggestion: start with a small % traffic to AWQ-quantized 7B behind Redwood routing with automatic fallback to FP16 13B if regression exceeds threshold.

Attachments / links: I've uploaded an initial trade-study worksheet and sample prompt set to the shared folder (attached + Drive link below).

Thanks for the clear summary, Marissa. Quick technical notes from the inference team about the AWQ / GPTQ / FP8 trade-offs you asked about — high level first, then concrete numbers from our sandbox runs (attached PDF).

High-level trade-offs:
- AWQ (aware weight quantization): excellent throughput improvement on 7B-class models with minimal architecture-specific retraining. Typically 2.5x-3.2x throughput vs FP16 on same GPU; quality degradation often small but workload-dependent — we recommend per-prompt-set evals.
- GPTQ (post-training quantization): well-supported for 13B variants; 4-bit GPTQ can give 3x cost improvement, but distribution shifts in summarization can expose hallucination/fluency regressions more than AWQ for some prompts.
- FP8 (hardware FP8 runtimes): near-FP16 quality for many workloads with 1.6x-2.2x throughput depending on kernel support; good middle ground if your GPUs support FP8 kernels.

Sandbox numbers (median of 10 runs on A10G-equivalent instances):
- Llama-3-13B FP16 baseline: 28 tokens/sec, median generation latency (1.2k tokens): 42s (not optimized for batching).
- 13B GPTQ (4-bit): 86 tokens/sec (x3.1), median gen latency: 14.5s. Quality: average BLEU/ROUGE drop ~1.8 pts on our internal summarization set.
- Redoak-7B AWQ: 72 tokens/sec (x2.6), median gen latency: 17.0s. Quality: avg ROUGE drop ~0.9 pts.
- 13B FP8 (where available): 52 tokens/sec (x1.85), median gen latency: 24.0s. Quality: ~0.4-0.8 pts drop.

Notes / recommendations:
- For Acme's latency SLO (99th 500ms) we'll likely need to combine quantization with sharding and continuous batching — Redwood routing can enforce SLOs while still routing overflow to higher-capacity variants.
- Run the full canonical prompt set to detect edge-case regressions; we recommend 500-1,000 prompts with the exact prompts you use in production to get representative results.
- We'll surface delta metrics per-prompt (not just averages) so you can triage prompts that regress more than threshold.

I've attached the initial benchmark PDF (benchmark_results_acme_20260225.pdf) and the trade-study workbook for tracking. If you'd like, I can join the tech deep-dive to walk through the kernel-level considerations.

—Rishi
Senior Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa / Rishi — very helpful. A couple quick clarifying Qs from our side so we can align evaluation criteria:

1) Quality threshold: we can tolerate up to 1.0 ROUGE point drop on average but want NO prompts with >3.0 pt drop (those we consider regressions that block rollouts). Is that feasible to detect with your plan?
2) For hallucination risk: are you surfacing model confidence or calibration signals per output? We need to know how you'll detect increased hallucination after quantization.
3) Timeline: can you share the estimated days to complete the 500-prompt run and produce the report? We need to align with procurement timelines.

Also: we cannot accept any model artifacts that were trained on patient-identifiable data — that constraints model selection if any model contains fine-tuning with PHI.

Happy to take the tech deep-dive next Tue or Wed mornings (PST).

Hi Alice — great questions. Quick answers and an updated plan: 

1) Detecting regressions: yes — we'll run per-prompt delta ROUGE/BLEU and flag any prompt with >3.0 pt drop as a hard fail. We also produce per-output calibration metrics (confidence, token-level perplexity proxies) and an AVH (automatic hallucination heuristic) score we use internally. We'll provide the code/notebooks for reproducibility.

2) Timeline: once we have your canonical prompt set (500 prompts), typical runtime for the full matrix (FP16 13B, 13B GPTQ, 7B AWQ, 13B FP8) is ~3 business days on our dedicated benchmarking pool (conservative estimate). We'll deliver the initial report and a short deck within 5 business days after run completion.

3) PHI constraints: understood — we'll restrict model choices to verified non-PHI-trained variants and document lineage in the report.
